_transcription: ENGLISH half only, CBSE Class 10 Science (086), set 31/4/3 (Series D4CBA/4), a follower of series 31/4 (reference 2024-31-4-1). plan.txt produced no skip list (no numbered cells in the Science scheme), so every question was matched to 31/4/1 by CONTENT on this paper's own page: 31 primary questions (and their OR alternatives) are 31/4/1's, reshuffled and renumbered, and their stem/context/options/answer/chapter/subtopic/difficulty are copied byte-for-byte from the reference; Q2, Q8, Q22, Q24, Q25, Q26, Q28, Q30, Q33, Q36(a) and Q36(b) are new to this set and transcribed fresh. 27 page images, idx 0-26 (cover announces 27 printed pages; last folio 27 on idx 26). idx 0 cover, idx 1 Hindi instructions, idx 2 English instructions + Q1-2; English on EVERY EVEN index 2-26, Hindi on every odd index 1-25 (each odd index is the Hindi of the page after it); odd-page tops checked, all Hindi, and every English page ends on a question boundary, so the parity holds throughout; idx 26 (last page) is English Q39. Instructions (i)-(vii) confirm sci80: 39 questions, A Q1-20 MCQ @1 (Q17-20 assertion-reason), B Q21-26 @2, C Q27-33 @3, D Q34-36 @5, E Q37-39 case-based @4. Instruction (viii) prints NO count of internal choices, so the roster was built by walking the marking scheme (ms idx 2-7, per-set, footer 'X SCIENCE 31/4/3 PAGE N' on every page, header '[ Paper Code: 31/4/3]'): bare OR after Q21, 23, 32, 34, 35, 36, 37(c), 38(c), 39(c) = 9 alternatives, each confirmed against a printed OR on the paper. Q30 prints parts (a) and (b) with NO OR between them (one 3-mark question, one row). Internal choices are labelled lower-case (a)/(b) and case studies (a), (b), (c)(i) OR (c)(ii), as on 31/4/1. All 20 Section-A answers are CBSE's own, read off the scheme page image (ms idx 2); each was re-derived and 19 agree; Q19 (31/4/1's Q17) disagrees (flagged, CBSE's B kept, as on the reference). No void note on any MCQ; one award-regardless note on Q38(b) (31/4/1's Q37(b), same note). Decimal points on this paper are RAISED dots (Q16 figure 0·5 Ω, Q26 1·6, Q36(a) 5·0 cm), written {\cdot}.

questions.stem:
A student fixes a sheet of white paper on a drawing board. He places a bar magnet in the centre of it. He sprinkles some iron filings uniformly around the bar magnet. Then he taps the drawing board gently and observes that the iron filings arrange themselves in a particular pattern.

(a) Why do iron filings arrange in a particular pattern ?

(b) What does the crowding of iron filings at the ends of the magnet indicate ?

(c) What do the lines, along which the iron filings align, represent ?

(d) If the student places a cardboard horizontally in a current carrying solenoid and repeats the above activity, in what pattern would the iron filings arrange ? State the conclusion drawn about the magnetic field based on the observed pattern of the lines.

(a) Name any two pairs of contrasting characters other than height used by Mendel in his experiments.

(b) On crossing a tall and a short pea plant, Mendel obtained \(\mathrm{F_1}\) generation in which all pea plants were tall.

(i) Are these plants exactly the same as tall plants of the parent generation ? Write their gene combination.

(ii) Give the percentage of short plants obtained in \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation when \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants are self-pollinated.

(iii) In what ratio would you find TT and Tt in \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation ?

Write the common name and the chemical name of the compound \(\mathrm{CaSO_4 \cdot \frac{1}{2}\,H_2O}\). Write the method of its preparation. Give chemical equation for the reaction, when water reacts with \(\mathrm{CaSO_4 \cdot \frac{1}{2}\,H_2O}\).
Explain with the help of a labelled diagram, the process of reproduction in Hydra by budding. Name the cells used for reproduction in this process.

List two roles of each of the following in human reproductive system :

(i) Seminal vesicles and prostate gland

(ii) Oviduct

(iii) Testis

Differentiate between biodegradable and non-biodegradable wastes. We generate a lot of non-biodegradable wastes in our daily life. Write any two harmful effects caused by these wastes if not disposed off properly.

questions.stem:
(i) Define a reflex arc. Why have reflex arcs evolved in animals ? Trace the sequence of events which occur, when you suddenly touch a hot object.

(ii) Name the part of nervous system which helps in communication between the central nervous system and other parts of the body. What are the two components of this system ?

(i) Leaves of ‘chhui-mui’ plant begin to fold up and droop in response to a stimulus. Name the stimulus and write the cause for such a rapid movement. Is there any growth involved in the movement ?

(ii) Define geotropism in plants. What is meant by positive and negative geotropism ? Give one example of each type.

questions.stem: What is a chemical reaction ? Describe one activity each to show that a chemical change has occurred in which (i) change of colour, and (ii) change in temperature has taken place.

(i) Define a decomposition reaction. How can we say that (I) electrolysis of water, and (II) blackening of silver bromide when exposed to sunlight, are decomposition reactions ? Mention the type of energy involved in each case.

(ii) “The type of reactions in which (I) calcium oxide is formed, and (II) calcium hydroxide is formed are opposite reactions to each other.” Justify this statement with the help of chemical equations.

(ii) Draw a ray diagram to show refraction of a ray of light through a rectangular glass slab. How is the emergent ray related to incident ray ? Mark lateral displacement in the diagram.
